anchor.statement: Proposition 4.2. The residuals R (0) θ , R (0) z in (4.12) are minus the cylindrical divergences ∂ r + 2/r and ∂r + 1/r of q −A−1/2 T 0 . In particular the equations for vanishing leading residual stress are −2L X ϕ XX + 2 ϕ X ϕ = S q , −2L(XU XX + U X ) = S n . (4.13)

correspondence.by: Christian Garry (drafted with Claude Code; second review by ChatGPT, checked)
correspondence.note: navierStokesResidual_tangential states that the two leading tangential residuals (with axial viscosity added back) equal minus the cylindrical divergences of the physical stress components, at points off the axis where f is nonzero. The stress-free equations (4.13) are not the conclusion of any declaration: the reader must set the stress coefficients to zero on an open radial interval (theta_eq_lag_minus_slope, axial_eq_lag_plus_slope), differentiate, substitute into angularLag_equation and axialLag_equation, and simplify with stressFree_angular_lag_algebra (and StressAlgebra.stressFree_axial_lag_algebra); that chain is the reviewer's argument.

links.doc:
Proposition 3.2 for the actual Cartesian Navier--Stokes residual.

The local hypotheses avoid extending the quotient defining radial velocity
across the axis. The two added terms are the exact axial-viscosity terms;
their explicit similarity formulas are `thetaAxialViscosity_eq` and
`axialAxialViscosity_eq`.
